The bonds were issued on March 6, 2026, in two tranches of ₹5,000 crore each with maturities of seven years and ten years, carrying coupon rates of 7.74% and 7.85% respectively. The bonds were listed on the BSE and NSE and received AAA (stable) ratings from CRISIL, ICRA, and India Ratings, indicating strong creditworthiness. The funds raised will be used exclusively for green and sustainable infrastructure projects such as renewable energy, energy efficiency, clean transportation, green buildings, pollution control, and climate change adaptation initiatives.

2026-03-07.question: Who set the Guinness World Record for the fastest 50m limbo skating with a time of 7.46 seconds in February 2025?
2026-03-07.explanation: Shrishti Dharmendra Sharma from India achieved a remarkable feat by setting the Guinness World Record for the fastest 50-meter limbo skating with a time of 7.46 seconds on February 28, 2025. The record was set at Sai Dham City in Maharashtra and involved skating under a series of descending horizontal poles without touching them. Limbo skating is a challenging sport that demands exceptional flexibility, balance, and speed. Sharma broke her own previous record of 9.59 seconds set in Italy in 2023. By improving her time by 2.13 seconds, she demonstrated extraordinary skill and control, further strengthening her position as a world leader in this unique sporting discipline.

2026-03-07.question: Which country announced a regional-first social media ban for minors under the age of 16 starting March 28, 2026?
2026-03-07.explanation: Indonesia has announced a new policy to restrict access to several social media platforms for minors under the age of 16. The initiative will begin on March 28, 2026, and will be implemented by the country’s Communications and Digital Ministry. The regulation targets major platforms such as TikTok, Facebook, Instagram, Threads, X, Bigo Live, Roblox, and YouTube, with a phased process of account deactivations for underage users. The move was introduced after the government declared a digital emergency to address issues such as cyberbullying, pornography, online fraud, and addiction caused by algorithm-driven content. The policy will initially operate through ministerial guidelines before permanent legislation establishing a minimum age requirement is introduced.

2026-03-07.question: Which Bengaluru-based space startup signed an MoU with Bharat Electronics Limited (BEL) to advance satellite technologies for Very Low Earth Orbit (VLEO)?
2026-03-07.explanation: Bellatrix Aerospace, a Bengaluru-based space startup, signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with Bharat Electronics Limited (BEL) in March 2026 to collaborate on the development of satellite systems and payloads designed for Very Low Earth Orbit (VLEO). This partnership focuses on building advanced satellite platforms capable of operating at altitudes between 100 and 450 kilometers above Earth. Satellites operating in VLEO offer several advantages, including higher-resolution Earth observation, lower communication latency, and improved atmospheric and climate data collection. Additionally, the natural orbital decay in VLEO reduces long-term space debris risks and lowers launch and operational costs compared to traditional orbits like LEO, MEO, and GEO.

2026-03-07.question: Which city deployed the AI-based “G-SPIDER” robot for hazardous canal maintenance to eliminate manual scavenging?
2026-03-07.explanation: The municipal corporation of Thiruvananthapuram introduced the AI-powered “G-SPIDER” robotic system to carry out hazardous canal maintenance and eliminate manual scavenging. Developed by Genrobotic Innovations, the robot operates using Cable-Driven Parallel Robotics along with a biomimetic claw that can grasp and remove irregular debris from canals. The initiative is part of the Swachh Bharat Mission–Urban 2.0, aiming to achieve completely human-free cleaning of the Amayizhanchan canal. The robot is equipped with artificial intelligence that identifies different types of waste in real time and transfers the extracted materials directly to collection vehicles, ensuring safer and more efficient waste management while preventing human exposure to toxic substances.

2026-03-07.question: Which accessibility technology company announced a global partnership with Accessibility Cloud to deliver AI-augmented, human-centred accessibility solutions at scale?
2026-03-07.explanation: AccessifyLabs, an accessibility technology company, announced a global strategic partnership with Accessibility Cloud, a Switzerland-based platform that provides detailed accessibility data through its API. The collaboration aims to improve digital accessibility by combining AI-driven automation with human-centered validation and remediation. AccessifyLabs contributes advanced tools such as AI-powered accessibility scanning, automated fixes, continuous monitoring, enterprise dashboards, and compliance reporting. Accessibility Cloud brings community-sourced data and API-based infrastructure that helps integrate accessibility information into websites, mobile applications, and physical-digital systems. Together, the partnership seeks to help organizations meet international accessibility standards such as WCAG 2.2, EN 301 549, ADA, and Section 508 while ensuring inclusive digital experiences.

2026-03-07.question: In which city did Shri Sanjay Seth inaugurate the Advanced Aadhaar Seva Kendra on March 6, 2026?
2026-03-07.explanation: The Advanced Aadhaar Seva Kendra (ASK) was inaugurated by Minister of State for Defence Shri Sanjay Seth on March 6, 2026, at Estate Plaza, Kantatoli in Ranchi. The centre was established to improve Aadhaar enrolment and update services by introducing upgraded hardware, high-speed connectivity, and better infrastructure. It aims to provide faster processing, greater transparency, and a more user-friendly experience for residents. Operated by Protean eGov Technologies Ltd under UIDAI guidelines, the centre supports both new enrolments and demographic or biometric updates. Its establishment also helps reduce waiting time and improve Aadhaar-related services for people in Ranchi and nearby districts.

2026-03-07.question: Which state has been announced as the host for the inaugural Khelo India Tribal Games 2026?
2026-03-07.explanation: The inaugural Khelo India Tribal Games 2026 will be hosted by the state of Chhattisgarh. The tournament is scheduled to take place from March 25 to April 6, 2026, across three major locations in the state of Raipur, Jagdalpur, and Sarguja. The event will feature seven medal sports, including athletics, football, hockey, weightlifting, archery, swimming, and wrestling, along with two demonstration sports, Mallakhamb and Kabaddi. The official mascot, named ‘Morveer’, symbolises the courage and cultural pride of India’s tribal communities. The games have also been declared an Event of National Importance and will follow international technical standards set by the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports.

2026-03-07.question: Which country approved the world’s first iPS stem-cell therapies for treating Parkinson’s disease and heart failure?
2026-03-07.explanation: Japan achieved a significant medical breakthrough by approving the world’s first commercial therapies derived from induced Pluripotent Stem (iPS) cells. One treatment, called Amchepry and developed by Sumitomo Pharma, focuses on Parkinson’s disease by transplanting stem-cell precursors into the brain to replace dopamine-producing cells that are lost in patients. Another therapy named ReHeart, developed by the startup Cuorips, uses heart muscle sheets to promote the formation of new blood vessels and improve heart function in patients with heart failure. These innovations build on the Nobel Prize-winning discovery of scientist Shinya Yamanaka in 2012, and both therapies are expected to become available to patients by Summer 2026.

2026-03-07.question: Which Indian cricketer became the first from India to be honoured with her own Barbie doll and join the Barbie Dream Team ahead of International Women’s Day 2026?
2026-03-07.explanation: Smriti Mandhana, the vice-captain of the Indian women’s cricket team, received a unique honour when Mattel created a Barbie doll in her likeness ahead of International Women’s Day on 8 March 2026. The doll was introduced as part of the Barbie Dream Team initiative and serves as a non-commercial tribute celebrating her achievements and role as an inspiration for young athletes. Mandhana has also made history by becoming the first Indian woman cricketer to score centuries in all three international formats—Tests, One Day Internationals, and T20 Internationals. This recognition highlights the growing global influence of Indian women’s cricket and encourages more girls to pursue sports professionally.

2026-03-06.question: Which international organisation partnered with NITI Aayog to improve nutrition and health outcomes in Aspirational Districts and Blocks across India?
2026-03-06.explanation: UNICEF partnered with NITI Aayog to improve nutrition and health outcomes in Aspirational Districts and Aspirational Blocks across India. The collaboration focuses on strengthening maternal and child nutrition, improving Anganwadi services, and enhancing health systems in underserved regions. The partnership also aims to promote multi-stakeholder engagement involving government agencies, private sector organisations, and local communities. Through this initiative, UNICEF will leverage its IMPAct4Nutrition platform to mobilise businesses and channel Corporate Social Responsibility funds toward nutrition programmes. The initiative supports the broader goals of the Aspirational Districts Programme, which seeks to improve socio-economic indicators in India’s most underdeveloped districts through better governance, monitoring, and service delivery.

2026-03-06.question: Which Indian state launched the MeHEALTH mobile app to help citizens access information about nearby hospitals, laboratories, and healthcare services?
2026-03-06.explanation: Kerala launched the MeHEALTH mobile application to improve public access to healthcare information and services. The app was introduced by the state Health Department to help citizens easily locate nearby hospitals, speciality departments, laboratories, blood banks, and pharmacies. It also provides features such as online doctor appointment booking and OP ticket generation, reducing waiting time at hospitals. Users can log in with their mobile number and generate a unique health ID using Aadhaar details. The app also integrates navigation features to guide users to healthcare institutions. This initiative strengthens digital healthcare access and enhances the efficiency of public health services across the state.

2026-03-06.question: In which Indian state did Union Home and Cooperation Minister Shri Amit Shah dedicate the IFFCO Sulphuric Acid Plant (SAP-III) and launch multiple cooperative sector initiatives on 6 March 2026?
2026-03-06.explanation: Union Home and Cooperation Minister Shri Amit Shah visited Paradip and Bhubaneswar on 6 March 2026 to dedicate the IFFCO Sulphuric Acid Plant (SAP-III) and launch several major cooperative sector initiatives. The programmes were organised in the state of Odisha and focused on strengthening cooperative institutions, promoting rural development, and boosting the agricultural and dairy sectors. The visit included the release of the State Cooperative Policy, launch of digital platforms, inauguration of Common Service Centres operated by PACS and LAMPS, and foundation stones for projects worth more than ₹3,275 crore. These initiatives aim to enhance rural prosperity, improve governance in cooperatives, and support farmers and producers through modern infrastructure and digital services.

2026-03-06.question: Which country became the first in the Americas to be verified by the WHO for eliminating leprosy as a public health problem?
2026-03-06.explanation: Chile achieved a major public health milestone by becoming the first country in the Americas and the fourth globally to receive official verification from the World Health Organisation for eliminating leprosy as a public health problem. This recognition was granted after the country maintained a prevalence rate of less than one case per 10,000 people at the national level for several consecutive years. The achievement reflects decades of consistent government commitment, strong integration of leprosy services into the public health system, and effective strategies such as early detection, multidrug therapy treatment coverage, surveillance, and contact tracing. High treatment completion rates and a very low proportion of cases among children further demonstrated successful control of disease transmission.

2026-03-06.question: By which year does the report project a major surge in obesity-related health conditions among Indian youth?
2026-03-06.explanation: A report warns that India may face a significant rise in obesity-related health problems among children and adolescents by the year 2030. The projections indicate a sharp increase in metabolic and cardiovascular conditions such as MASLD (Metabolic dysfunction–associated steatotic liver disease), high triglycerides, hypertension, and hyperglycemia. These conditions are linked to lifestyle changes, including increased consumption of ultra-processed foods, reduced physical activity, and rising sedentary habits due to screen time and urban lifestyles. India is experiencing a rapid nutrition transition along with a “double burden” where undernutrition and overnutrition coexist. If preventive measures are not strengthened, these early health risks could lead to a substantial increase in heart disease, diabetes, and liver disorders in adulthood.

2026-03-06.question: On which river will India build its first riverine lighthouses under the National Waterway-2 project?
2026-03-06.explanation: The Brahmaputra River is the river where India will establish its first riverine lighthouses as part of the National Waterway-2 project. The initiative includes the construction of four solar-powered lighthouses at Pandu, Bogibeel, Silghat, and Biswanath Ghat with an investment of ₹84 crore. Each lighthouse will be approximately 20 metres tall and will help guide vessels during nighttime and challenging weather conditions. The project is implemented by the Directorate General of Lighthouses and Lightships in partnership with the Inland Waterways Authority of India. It aims to improve navigation safety, boost cargo movement, such as tea and fertiliser, and promote tourism along the Brahmaputra river corridor in Northeast India.

2026-03-06.question: Which Indian state government announced a ₹25,000 incentive for couples having a second or third child to address declining fertility rates?
2026-03-06.explanation: Andhra Pradesh introduced a policy providing a ₹25,000 financial incentive for couples who have a second or third child. The initiative was announced by Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu to address the state’s declining Total Fertility Rate (TFR), which is currently around 1.5, below the replacement level of 2.1 required for stable population growth. The policy aims to encourage families to have more children and maintain demographic balance while addressing concerns about an ageing population and future workforce shortages. It also reflects a shift from earlier family planning policies toward population growth management, ensuring long-term socio-economic stability in the state.

2026-03-06.question: Which Indian company was selected as the official partner for UNESCO’s World Engineering Day for Sustainable Development 2026?
2026-03-06.explanation: Adani Group was selected as the official partner for UNESCO’s World Engineering Day for Sustainable Development (WED) 2026. This recognition marks the first time an Indian organization has been chosen for this global partnership coordinated by the World Federation of Engineering Organizations under UNESCO. The selection highlights the company’s contributions to renewable energy and sustainable engineering solutions. A major factor behind this recognition is the massive Khavda Renewable Energy Project in Gujarat, being developed by Adani Green Energy Limited. The project aims to reach a capacity of 30 GW by 2029, making it one of the largest renewable energy projects in the world and supporting India’s clean energy goals.

2026-03-06.question: Who was reappointed as the Drugs Controller General of India (DCGI) for an additional one-year term as approved by the Appointments Committee of the Cabinet (ACC) in March 2026?
2026-03-06.explanation: Dr. Rajeev Raghuvanshi received approval from the Appointments Committee of the Cabinet (ACC) for reappointment as the Drugs Controller General of India (DCGI) for an additional one-year term in March 2026. He was initially appointed in November 2023 on a contractual basis for two years with the possibility of extension. The extension ensures continuity in leadership at the Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation (CDSCO), India’s apex drug regulatory authority. With prior experience as Joint Drugs Controller (India) and other senior roles within CDSCO, Dr. Raghuvanshi brings significant expertise in regulatory science, pharmacovigilance, and biologics regulation, supporting ongoing reforms and global harmonisation efforts in India’s pharmaceutical regulatory system.

2026-03-06.question: In which city was the official logo of the world’s first franchise-based “Cycling League of India” unveiled by Union Minister Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya on March 5, 2026?
2026-03-06.explanation: Union Minister for Youth Affairs and Sports, Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya, unveiled the official logo of the Cycling League of India (CLI) on March 5, 2026, in New Delhi. The league is recognised as the world’s first franchise-based professional cycling league and aims to promote cycling as a major competitive sport in India. Inspired by franchise models similar to those used in popular cricket leagues, the initiative is designed to encourage grassroots talent, improve professional opportunities for cyclists, and strengthen India’s presence in global cycling competitions. The league will feature city-based teams, professional riders, youth talents, women’s categories, and multiple race formats, including road races, criteriums, and time trials.

2026-03-06.question: In which Indian state was the 5th cohort of the HerSTART initiative launched by the Chief Minister to support women-led startups?
2026-03-06.explanation: Gujarat is the state where the 5th cohort of the HerSTART initiative was launched by Chief Minister Bhupendra Patel to strengthen women entrepreneurship and innovation-driven growth. The programme supports women-led startups by providing mentoring, funding opportunities, and connections to investor networks. Selected entrepreneurs also receive assistance such as co-working spaces, legal and intellectual property advisory, branding support, and market linkages. Along with the launch of the cohort, a modern Research Park was inaugurated to promote collaboration between academia and industry. The initiative focuses on sectors including technology, health-tech, agri-tech, sustainability, and social enterprises to accelerate the growth of scalable women-led ventures.

2026-03-05.question: Who assumed charge as the Director General of Naval Armament (DGONA) at Naval Headquarters, New Delhi, on March 1, 2026?
2026-03-05.explanation: B.P. Singh, a 1994-batch officer of the Indian Naval Armament Service (INAS), assumed charge as the Director General of Naval Armament (DGONA) at Naval Headquarters in New Delhi on March 1, 2026. He succeeded Divakar Jayant, who retired on February 28, 2026, after completing a distinguished career. Before taking up this position, B.P. Singh served as the Chief General Manager of the Naval Armament Depot (NAD) Mumbai, where he handled operational, logistics, and infrastructure responsibilities. He also held key roles at NAD Aluva, Visakhapatnam, Mumbai, and Trombay, contributing significantly to naval armament management and operational efficiency.

2026-03-05.question: Which country renewed a $75 billion bilateral currency swap agreement with India for an additional three years starting March 4, 2026?
2026-03-05.explanation: Japan renewed its $75 billion bilateral currency swap agreement with India for another three years beginning March 4, 2026. The arrangement was formalised through an exchange of letters between the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) and the Bank of Japan (BoJ). This financial mechanism allows either country to access the other’s currency—Japanese yen or Indian rupee—during times of balance-of-payments pressure or liquidity shortages. The agreement, originally established in 2018 and renewed earlier in 2023, strengthens financial cooperation between the two nations and serves as a safeguard to maintain macroeconomic stability and enhance investor confidence during global economic uncertainties.

2026-03-05.question: Who was appointed as the first Kashmiri woman Superintendent of Srinagar Central Jail in March 2026?
2026-03-05.explanation: Saba Shawl was appointed as the Superintendent of Srinagar Central Jail in March 2026, becoming the first Kashmiri woman to hold this position in the history of the facility. Her appointment represents an important step toward greater gender representation in Jammu and Kashmir’s prison administration. Srinagar Central Jail is one of the oldest and most significant correctional institutions in the Union Territory, housing both undertrial prisoners and convicts. As a senior officer in the J&K Prison Department, Saba Shawl has previously served in several roles, gaining extensive experience in jail administration, inmate welfare, and security management.

2026-03-05.question: In which city was the 11th edition of the Raisina Dialogue held from March 5–7, 2026?
2026-03-05.explanation: The 11th edition of the Raisina Dialogue was held from March 5–7, 2026, in New Delhi, India. It is organised by the Observer Research Foundation (ORF) in partnership with the Ministry of External Affairs. The Raisina Dialogue is regarded as Asia’s premier conference on geopolitics and geoeconomics, bringing together global leaders, policymakers, scholars, and experts from various sectors. The 2026 theme was “Saṁskāra – Assertion, Accommodation, Advancement.” The event featured discussions on global governance, climate challenges, technological developments, and economic resilience. Finland’s President Alexander Stubb attended as the chief guest and delivered the keynote address.

2026-03-05.question: Which Indian state launched the ₹12.66 crore Challenge Fund to accelerate rural entrepreneurship, focusing on women and youth?
2026-03-05.explanation: Telangana introduced a ₹12.66 crore Challenge Fund to promote rural entrepreneurship, particularly among women and youth at the grassroots level. The initiative is implemented through the Society for Elimination of Rural Poverty (SERP) in collaboration with TBIS BITS Pilani Hyderabad, T-Hub, and WE Hub, with support from the Ministry of Rural Development. It aims to transition about 65 lakh Self-Help Group (SHG) women from microfinance participation to formal entrepreneurship and scalable ventures. Around 300 selected entrepreneurs will receive mentoring, enterprise diagnostics, branding support, market access, and help in accessing finance. The programme will be implemented across all 33 districts through a decentralised outreach model.

2026-03-05.question: Who was named to TIME’s Women of the Year 2026 list for her transformative work in advancing girls’ education in rural India?
2026-03-05.explanation: Safeena Husain, the founder of the non-profit organisation Educate Girls, was included in TIME magazine’s Women of the Year 2026 list for her impactful efforts in promoting girls’ education in rural India. Her initiative has helped bring more than 2 million out-of-school girls back into the education system. What began in 2007 with work in about 50 villages in Rajasthan has expanded significantly to over 25,000 villages across Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, and Uttar Pradesh. In 2025, Educate Girls also received the Ramon Magsaysay Award for community leadership. Her work highlights the importance of grassroots initiatives in improving educational access for marginalised girls.

2026-03-05.question: In which city was the AI-powered ‘Saksham Skill Survey’ launched to map and upskill youth through a door-to-door drive?
2026-03-05.explanation: The AI-powered ‘Saksham Skill Survey’ was launched in Mumbai, specifically in the H-West ward covering areas such as Bandra, Khar, and Santacruz. The initiative aims to assess the education levels, skills, and employment potential of youth aged between 18 and 40 years. Around 55,000 households will be covered through door-to-door enumeration. The project intends to train at least 15,000 individuals and help about 5,000 achieve self-reliance through employment or entrepreneurship. Conducted by Sapio Analytics, the survey collects data on educational qualifications, skills, and training needs, and uses artificial intelligence to develop a decentralised workforce intelligence model.

2026-03-05.question: On which date is the International Day for Disarmament and Non-Proliferation Awareness observed every year?
2026-03-05.explanation: The International Day for Disarmament and Non-Proliferation Awareness is observed annually on March 5. The day was proclaimed by the United Nations General Assembly through Resolution A/RES/77/51 to raise awareness about the importance of disarmament, arms control, and non-proliferation in maintaining global peace and security. It encourages governments, UN agencies, civil society organisations, educational institutions, and the media to conduct awareness activities. The observance also emphasises educating young people about the risks associated with weapons of mass destruction, illegal arms trade, and emerging military technologies, while promoting dialogue, peacebuilding, and international cooperation to reduce armed conflict worldwide.

2026-03-05.question: Which institution signed a five-year Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the Survey of India for geospatial research and innovation?
2026-03-05.explanation: Survey of India (SoI) signed a five-year Memorandum of Understanding with Kerala University of Digital Sciences, Innovation and Technology, popularly known as Kerala Digital University. The collaboration aims to strengthen geospatial research and promote digital innovation by leveraging advanced technologies such as geoinformatics, artificial intelligence, and machine learning. The partnership focuses on improving the collection, processing, analysis, and application of geospatial data. It also includes joint research and development activities, capacity-building programs, training initiatives, and higher education opportunities. This initiative is expected to support technological advancement and enhance expertise in geospatial technologies and digital sciences in India.

2026-03-05.question: In which Indian state was the ‘HANUMAN’ project launched to mitigate human–wildlife conflict?
2026-03-05.explanation: The ‘HANUMAN’ project (Healing and Nurturing Units for Monitoring, Aid and Nursing of Wildlife) was launched in Andhra Pradesh on March 3, 2026, by Deputy Chief Minister and Forest and Environment Minister Pawan Kalyan. The initiative aims to address the growing issue of human–wildlife conflict caused by expanding human settlements near forest areas and increased wildlife movement into rural regions. As part of the rollout, more than 100 specially equipped vehicles, including rapid response units and wildlife ambulances, were deployed. The project focuses on early warning systems, real-time monitoring, quick rescue operations, and rehabilitation efforts to reduce casualties, crop damage, and retaliatory harm to wildlife.

2026-03-04.question: Which country has overtaken the United States to become the second-highest country globally for childhood obesity according to the World Obesity Atlas 2026?
2026-03-04.explanation: India has surpassed the United States to become the country with the second-highest number of children affected by obesity globally, according to the World Obesity Atlas 2026 released by the World Obesity Federation. The report indicates that around 41 million Indian children had a high Body Mass Index (BMI) by 2025, including about 14 million living with obesity. Projections suggest that by 2040, nearly 20 million children in India may be living with obesity, and around 56 million could be overweight or obese. Rising consumption of sugary beverages, low physical activity among adolescents, and limited access to nutritious food are among the key factors contributing to this growing public health challenge.

2026-03-04.question: In whose presence were the ₹5,083 crore defence contracts for ALH Mk-III helicopters and VL-Shtil missiles signed at South Block, New Delhi, in March 2026?
2026-03-04.explanation: The Ministry of Defence signed major defence procurement contracts worth ₹5,083 crore on March 3, 2026, aimed at strengthening India’s maritime security and air defence capabilities. The agreements included the purchase of six ALH Mk-III (Maritime Role) helicopters for the Indian Coast Guard and VL-Shtil surface-to-air missiles for the Indian Navy. These contracts were signed at South Block, New Delhi, in the presence of Defence Secretary Rajesh Kumar Singh. The ALH Mk-III deal with Hindustan Aeronautics Limited supports indigenous manufacturing under the “Buy (Indian-IDDM)” category, while the VL-Shtil missile agreement with Russia’s Rosoboronexport enhances the layered air defence system of Indian naval warships.

2026-03-04.question: On which date is National Safety Day observed annually in India to promote workplace safety and accident prevention?
2026-03-04.explanation: National Safety Day is observed every year in India on March 4 to promote awareness about workplace safety, occupational health, and accident prevention. The day is organised by the National Safety Council (NSC), which was established on March 4, 1966. National Safety Day was first celebrated in 1972 and has since grown into a nationwide campaign encouraging industries and organizations to adopt better safety practices. The observance now extends into National Safety Week and even National Safety Month, during which seminars, safety drills, training programs, and awareness campaigns are conducted to strengthen safety culture across workplaces and protect employees from occupational hazards.

2026-03-04.question: On which date is World Obesity Day observed globally to raise awareness about the growing obesity crisis?
2026-03-04.explanation: World Obesity Day is observed annually on March 4 to raise awareness about the global obesity crisis and encourage collective action to address this major public health challenge. Established by the World Obesity Federation in 2015, the observance was originally held on October 11 but was moved to March 4 in 2020 to align with other global health initiatives. The day focuses on promoting healthier lifestyles, improving access to nutritious food, and encouraging physical activity. It also highlights that obesity is a complex chronic disease influenced by genetic, environmental, social, and economic factors, requiring coordinated efforts from governments, healthcare professionals, and communities.

2026-03-04.question: Which country became the first in the United Kingdom to legalise water cremation (alkaline hydrolysis) as a greener alternative to traditional burial and cremation?
2026-03-04.explanation: Scotland became the first country in the United Kingdom to legalise water cremation, also known as alkaline hydrolysis. This method is considered an environmentally friendly alternative to traditional cremation and burial because it produces significantly lower carbon emissions. The process involves placing the body in a pressurized chamber with water and potassium hydroxide, which breaks down soft tissues while leaving bones that are later returned to families as powdered remains. The reform represents one of the most significant changes to cremation laws since 1902, and the first water cremations are expected to begin by summer 2026 after necessary approvals.

2026-03-04.question: The Indian Army signed an MoU with the Forest Department of which region on World Wildlife Day 2026 to protect the Snow Leopard and other high-altitude wildlife?
2026-03-04.explanation: The Indian Army and the Ladakh Forest Department signed a Memorandum of Understanding to strengthen wildlife conservation efforts in fragile high-altitude ecosystems. The initiative focuses on protecting species such as the Snow Leopard, Himalayan Wolf, Bharal (Blue Sheep), Ibex, Himalayan Marmot, and the Black-necked Crane. The agreement also includes the establishment of a Joint Snow Leopard Conservation Cell to monitor wildlife and coordinate conservation actions. Ladakh’s cold desert environment, characterised by low oxygen levels, extreme temperatures, and sparse vegetation, makes its biodiversity highly vulnerable, making this collaborative conservation effort particularly important.

2026-03-03.question: Which institution formalised a Framework for Action with the International Solar Alliance (ISA) to advance solar skills and capacity building across member countries?
2026-03-03.explanation: The International Solar Alliance (ISA) signed a Framework for Action with IIT Delhi to strengthen collaboration in renewable energy, particularly in human resource development, academic programmes, joint research, and knowledge exchange. This agreement builds upon five years of successful partnership, including the ISA-supported M.Tech programme in Renewable Energy Technologies & Management, which has trained over 100 mid-career professionals from regions such as Africa, Asia-Pacific, and Small Island Developing States. The expanded framework introduces new training models, trainer development initiatives, and broader capacity-building measures to accelerate solar adoption and promote clean energy transitions across ISA’s member countries.

2026-03-03.question: Which state government signed an MoU with GIZ and the State Mission for Clean Ganga (SMCG) to develop basin-based masterplans for the Ichhamati and Jalangi rivers?
2026-03-03.explanation: The Government of West Bengal entered into a Memorandum of Understanding with GIZ, the German development agency, and the State Mission for Clean Ganga (SMCG) to prepare comprehensive basin-based masterplans for the Ichhamati and Jalangi river basins. These rivers are significant transboundary distributaries in the Ganga delta, flowing between India and Bangladesh. The initiative aims to ensure sustainable river basin management by addressing ecological degradation, water security challenges, and socio-economic concerns. It also aligns with the objectives of the National Mission for Clean Ganga, while incorporating German expertise in climate resilience, integrated river basin management, and environmental sustainability.

2026-03-03.question: When will World Wildlife Day 2026 be observed globally?
2026-03-03.explanation: World Wildlife Day 2026 will be observed on March 3, marking the anniversary of the signing of the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora (CITES) in 1973. The day is dedicated to celebrating wild animals and plants while promoting global biodiversity conservation efforts. The 2026 theme focuses on “Medicinal and Aromatic Plants: Conserving Health, Heritage and Livelihoods,” emphasising the importance of plant species in healthcare, cultural traditions, and sustainable economies. The observance highlights the urgent need to protect ecosystems, regulate wildlife trade, and address threats such as habitat destruction and climate change.

2026-03-03.question: Which country announced a Strategic Energy Partnership with India and agreed on a CAD 2.6 billion uranium supply deal in March 2026?
2026-03-03.explanation: Canada entered into a Strategic Energy Partnership with India as part of a broader roadmap to reset bilateral relations. The partnership covers cooperation in clean energy, conventional energy, civil nuclear power, and critical minerals. A major highlight was a CAD 2.6 billion uranium supply agreement between Cameco and India’s Department of Atomic Energy, strengthening India’s nuclear energy capacity. Both nations also relaunched ministerial energy dialogues and initiated negotiations for a Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA) to boost bilateral trade to CAD 70 billion by 2030, reinforcing long-term economic and strategic collaboration.

2026-03-03.question: Which state issued a Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) for Heat Wave Management for Higher Education Institutions ahead of the summer season?
2026-03-03.explanation: The Higher Education Department of Odisha released a Standard Operating Procedure for Heat Wave Management applicable to colleges and universities across the state as part of its summer preparedness strategy. The directive focuses on safeguarding students, faculty, and staff from extreme heat conditions. Key measures include rescheduling classes and examinations to morning hours, restricting outdoor academic and sports activities during peak afternoon heat, ensuring uninterrupted access to safe drinking water, and maintaining first aid readiness for heat-related illnesses. The initiative reflects proactive governance aimed at minimising health risks during intense summer heatwaves.

2026-03-03.question: Which institution signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with HCLTech to drive deep tech innovation for Global Capability Centres (GCCs)?
2026-03-03.explanation: HCLTech collaborated with IIT Kanpur through a Memorandum of Understanding to promote research-led innovation in deep technology domains for Global Capability Centres (GCCs). The partnership aims to convert cutting-edge academic research into practical pilots and scalable solutions. Key focus areas include artificial intelligence, robotics, advanced engineering, and next-generation technologies. This collaboration positions HCLTech as a strategic enabler for GCCs, helping them accelerate research and development, gain access to specialised expertise, and reduce time-to-market without the need to establish dedicated in-house research facilities.

2026-03-03.question: Where did the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) unveil the indigenous 30 kW Wide Band Gap-based Integrated Drive System for electric vehicles on March 3, 2026?
2026-03-03.explanation: The Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) unveiled the indigenously developed 30 kW Wide Band Gap-based Integrated Drive System for electric vehicles in Chennai. The launch took place at IIT Madras under the National Mission on Power Electronics Technology (NaMPET). The system was jointly developed by C-DAC Thiruvananthapuram, IIT Madras, and industry partner Lucas TVS. This innovation enhances India’s capabilities in advanced power electronics and supports the rapidly growing electric passenger vehicle market. It also contributes to reducing dependence on imported high-performance electric vehicle components, strengthening the country’s push toward technological self-reliance.

2026-03-03.question: Which state exported its first consignment of GI-tagged Karbi Anglong Ginger to London, United Kingdom?
2026-03-03.explanation: Assam marked a significant milestone in agricultural exports by dispatching its first-ever shipment of GI-tagged Karbi Anglong Ginger to London. The consignment was flagged off by the state’s Agriculture Minister at Krishi Bhawan in Guwahati. Karbi Anglong Ginger, which received its Geographical Indication tag in 2015, is known for its distinct aroma, flavour, and superior quality resulting from the region’s unique agro-climatic conditions. Cultivated using traditional Jhum and Tila farming systems in the Singhasan Hills, this export initiative aims to boost farmer incomes, strengthen global market access, and enhance the international recognition of the state’s agricultural produce.

2026-03-03.question: Who assumed charge as the Director General of Naval Armament (DGONA) at Naval Headquarters on March 1, 2026?
2026-03-03.explanation: B.P. Singh took over as the Director General of Naval Armament (DGONA) at Naval Headquarters in New Delhi on March 1, 2026. A senior officer from the 1994 batch of the Indian Naval Armament Service, he succeeded Divakar Jayant following his retirement. With over three decades of experience in naval armament management, procurement, logistics, and guided weapon systems, he has held key positions at multiple Naval Armament Depots and at Naval Headquarters. An alumnus of the National Defence College, he brings strategic and operational expertise to strengthen India’s naval weapon systems management and maritime defence preparedness.

2026-03-03.question: Who was appointed by the Government of India as the Interim Chairman & Managing Director (CMD) of Engineers India Limited (EIL) effective March 1, 2026?
2026-03-03.explanation: The Government of India appointed Praveen M. Khanooja to hold additional charge as Chairman & Managing Director of Engineers India Limited (EIL) beginning March 1, 2026. The appointment, approved by the Minister of Petroleum & Natural Gas, is for three months or until a regular CMD assumes office. A 1994-batch officer of the Indian Audit & Accounts Service, he continues serving as Additional Secretary in the Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas while handling CMD responsibilities. His extensive experience spans defence audit, railways audit, central government finance, and leadership roles in key petroleum and economic intelligence institutions.

2026-03-02.question: Which Indian state has established its first Dark Sky Park at Ariyur Shola Reserve Forest in Kolli Hills to promote astrotourism and preserve the night sky?
2026-03-02.explanation: Tamil Nadu has set up its first Dark Sky Park at Ariyur Shola Reserve Forest in the Kolli Hills of Namakkal district. The initiative focuses on preserving the natural darkness of the night sky by reducing light pollution, thereby creating ideal conditions for astronomical observation. It also aims to promote astrotourism, educate visitors about celestial bodies such as constellations and planets, and raise awareness about the adverse effects of artificial lighting. Additionally, the project encourages sustainable eco-tourism that supports local tribal communities while ensuring the protection of the surrounding forest ecosystem.

2026-03-02.question: Which country’s first-ever Blue Bond, issued by DFCC Bank, was dually listed on NSE International Exchange at GIFT City?
2026-03-02.explanation: Sri Lanka is the country whose DFCC Bank issued the first-ever Blue Bond that was dually listed on the NSE International Exchange at GIFT City. The LKR 3 billion bond was initially listed on the Colombo Stock Exchange before being admitted to trading under GIFT City’s offshore regulatory framework. Blue bonds are a specialised subset of green bonds that channel investments into ocean conservation, sustainable fisheries, marine ecosystem protection, and water security projects. The dual listing enhances global investor participation and strengthens the country’s presence in sustainable and innovative financial markets.

2026-03-02.question: In which city was Micron’s first India ATMP (Assembly, Test, Mark & Pack) semiconductor plant inaugurated by Prime Minister Narendra Modi?
2026-03-02.explanation: Sanand is the city where Micron Semiconductor Technology India Pvt Ltd established its first Assembly, Test, Mark & Pack (ATMP) facility in India. The plant was inaugurated by Prime Minister Narendra Modi and marks the beginning of commercial production of made-in-India semiconductor memory modules. With an investment exceeding ₹22,500 crore, the project is a major milestone under the India Semiconductor Mission. The facility includes around 500,000 square feet of cleanroom space and is designed to process imported DRAM and NAND wafers into finished memory products, strengthening India’s role in the global semiconductor value chain.

2026-03-02.question: In which Indian state was the new blind groundwater fish species ‘Gitchak nakana’ discovered in a dug-out well?
2026-03-02.explanation: Assam is the state where the new blind groundwater fish species ‘Gitchak nakana’ was discovered in Goalpara district. This remarkable finding marks the first recorded instance of a groundwater-dwelling fish from Northeast India and the broader Eastern Himalayan region. The tiny, translucent red fish measures about 2 cm in length and exhibits classic subterranean adaptations such as complete blindness, lack of pigmentation, and absence of a skull roof. Found in underground aquifers rather than caves, the discovery highlights the rich yet fragile biodiversity of the Brahmaputra Valley and underscores the need for groundwater conservation.

2026-03-02.question: In which city was the National Conference on UDISE+ organised by the Department of School Education & Literacy in February 2026?
2026-03-02.explanation: Bhubaneswar hosted the two-day National Conference on Unified District Information System for Education Plus (UDISE+), organised by the Department of School Education & Literacy under the Ministry of Education in collaboration with the Government of Odisha. The conference focused on enhancing the reliability, real-time accuracy, and strategic use of UDISE+, which serves as India’s flagship education data platform. Discussions centred on strengthening data integrity, resolving implementation challenges faced by states and union territories, and expanding the system into an AI-compliant decision support framework to enable evidence-based policymaking and effective implementation of Samagra Shiksha and NEP 2020 initiatives.

2026-03-02.question: Which team won their maiden Ranji Trophy title in the 2025-26 season by defeating Karnataka in the final?
2026-03-02.explanation: Jammu & Kashmir secured its first-ever Ranji Trophy title in the 2025–26 season, marking a historic achievement after 67 years of participation in India’s premier domestic first-class cricket tournament. The team defeated Karnataka in the final held at the KSCA Rajnagar Stadium in Hubballi. This victory is regarded as a transformative milestone for cricket in the Union Territory, symbolising resilience, consistent talent development, and competitive growth. The Ranji Trophy, organized annually by the BCCI since 1934–35, features teams from states and union territories across India, making this triumph especially significant.

2026-03-02.question: Which city set a new Guinness World Record by planting 2,51,446 saplings in one hour on 1 March 2026?
2026-03-02.explanation: Varanasi achieved a historic milestone by planting 2,51,446 saplings within a single hour, surpassing the previous record held by China for eight years. The large-scale plantation drive was conducted on 350 bighas of land in Domari village along the banks of the Ganga. Around 20,000 participants took part in the synchronised effort, which was officially verified by a Guinness World Records judge. The area has been structured into 60 sectors named after prominent Kashi ghats, creating a symbolic urban forest using the Miyawaki method to promote rapid ecological restoration and biodiversity conservation.

2026-03-02.question: Which payments company partnered with Gnani.ai to launch an agentic AI platform enabling in-call UPI payments during live customer conversations?
2026-03-02.explanation: Gnani.ai collaborated with Razorpay to introduce an innovative agentic AI collections platform that enables customers to complete UPI payments during live calls without disconnecting or switching to external links. The platform combines Gnani.ai’s advanced AI systems, capable of handling over 10 million calls daily, with Razorpay’s Model Context Protocol (MCP) server to create a seamless, real-time payment interface. This deployment represents one of India’s first production-level uses of autonomous AI agents executing financial transactions, significantly enhancing operational efficiency for enterprises in sectors such as BFSI, telecom, utilities, and e-commerce.

2026-03-02.question: Which organisation provided a USD 150 million direct loan and acted as the mandated lead arranger for IIFL Home Finance’s USD 300 million financing package?
2026-03-02.explanation: The USD 300 million financing agreement was structured to expand affordable housing loans, particularly targeting women borrowers from economically weaker and lower-middle-income groups. Out of the total amount, USD 150 million was provided directly by the Asian Development Bank, while the remaining USD 150 million was raised through parallel loans from institutions such as MUFG, Emirates NBD, Sampath Bank, and Hatton National Bank. The Asian Development Bank also served as the mandated lead arranger and bookrunner for the entire package, highlighting its key role in promoting financial inclusion, women’s empowerment, and sustainable urban development in India.

2026-03-02.question: In which Indian state has GAIL approved a ₹1,736 crore greenfield wind power project as part of its renewable energy expansion?
2026-03-02.explanation: Maharashtra is the state where GAIL (India) Limited has approved a ₹1,736 crore investment for a greenfield wind power project. This initiative represents the company’s largest single renewable energy investment so far and reflects its strategic transition toward becoming an integrated energy player. The proposed wind farm is expected to have a capacity of around 300–350 MW, with construction likely to begin in 2026–27 and commercial operations targeted for 2028–29. The project supports GAIL’s goal of achieving nearly 2 GW of renewable capacity by 2030 and contributes to India’s broader non-fossil fuel energy ambitions.

2026-03-02.question: Which bank received RBI approval for SBI Mutual Fund to acquire up to a 9.99% stake through its various schemes?
2026-03-02.explanation: Bandhan Bank is the institution in which SBI Mutual Fund has been permitted by the Reserve Bank of India to acquire up to a 9.99% stake. The approval allows SBI Mutual Fund to become one of the largest non-promoter shareholders in the bank, signalling strong institutional confidence in its performance and future prospects. The investment reflects optimism regarding improvements in asset quality, expansion of its retail franchise, and overall growth strategy. This development is expected to strengthen the bank’s shareholding structure, improve investor sentiment, and support its long-term capital-raising and expansion initiatives.

2026-03-01.question: Which digital payments company launched an AI-powered natural language search feature built on Microsoft Foundry?
2026-03-01.explanation: PhonePe introduced an AI-powered natural language search feature built on Microsoft Foundry, transforming how users interact with the app. The feature enables customers to make payments, recharge FASTag, check gold prices, and track transactions using simple voice or text commands. Designed with a hybrid AI model combining on-device and cloud inferencing, it ensures strong privacy safeguards and secure data handling. The conversational interface replaces traditional menu-based navigation with intent-driven routing, making digital payments more intuitive and personalised. With millions of users and merchants across India, this innovation significantly enhances convenience and accessibility in fintech services.

2026-03-01.question: Which state government announced the launch of CM Shri Schools on the lines of the PM Shri Schools initiative?
2026-03-01.explanation: Haryana has announced the launch of CM Shri Schools, modelled on the central government’s PM Shri Schools initiative to enhance the quality of state-run education. The new schools will follow the CBSE curriculum pattern, ensuring structured academic standards, skill-based learning, and improved preparation for competitive examinations. The initiative also emphasizes modern infrastructure and better learning outcomes. Additionally, the state continues to implement 25% reservation for Economically Weaker Sections under the Right to Education Act, promoting inclusive access to quality education. This combined reform approach aims to strengthen educational standards and equity across the state.

2026-03-01.question: Which state government launched the ‘Meri Rasoi’ scheme to provide free food kits to 40 lakh blue card holder families?
2026-03-01.explanation: Punjab launched the ‘Meri Rasoi’ scheme to provide free food kits to nearly 40 lakh economically weaker families holding blue cards. The initiative, announced by Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann ahead of the state’s Budget Session, aims to address nutritional gaps among low-income households. Under the first phase from April to June 2026, beneficiaries will receive essential items such as chana dal, sugar, iodized salt, turmeric powder, and mustard oil. The scheme focuses on improving child health, reducing malnutrition, strengthening food security, and ensuring that vulnerable families receive balanced and nutritious food supplies regularly.

2026-03-01.question: On which date is National Science Day observed every year in India to honour the discovery of the Raman Effect?
2026-03-01.explanation: February 28 is observed annually as National Science Day in India to commemorate the discovery of the Raman Effect by Sir C. V. Raman in 1928. This groundbreaking work explained the scattering of light through transparent materials and later earned him the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1930, making him the first Asian Nobel laureate in science. The Government of India officially designated this date as National Science Day in 1986. The occasion promotes scientific awareness, innovation, and research culture, while celebrating India’s significant contributions to global scientific advancement and encouraging future generations in STEM fields.

2026-03-01.question: Who has taken additional charge as the Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of NITI Aayog?
2026-03-01.explanation: Nidhi Chhibber has taken additional charge as the Chief Executive Officer of NITI Aayog following the completion of BVR Subrahmanyam’s three-year term in February 2026. A 1994-batch IAS officer of the Chhattisgarh cadre, she currently serves as Director General of the Development Monitoring and Evaluation Office (DMEO) under NITI Aayog. She has also previously held the position of Chairperson of the Central Board of Secondary Education. Her extensive experience in policy monitoring, evaluation, and education sector reforms positions her to strengthen data-driven governance and performance assessment within India’s premier policy think tank.

2026-03-01.question: Which country signed a new MoU with India to strengthen cooperation in forests, wildlife, biodiversity conservation, and climate change?
2026-03-01.explanation: Nepal signed a new Memorandum of Understanding with India to enhance bilateral cooperation in forests, wildlife protection, biodiversity conservation, and climate change mitigation. The agreement focuses on restoring transboundary wildlife corridors, protecting key species such as tigers, elephants, rhinoceroses, and snow leopards, and strengthening protected area management. It also emphasises combating wildlife crime, improving coordination between enforcement agencies, and promoting capacity building for frontline forest staff. Given the shared ecosystems and migratory wildlife habitats across borders, the partnership supports integrated conservation strategies and climate resilience efforts in the Himalayan and adjoining landscapes.

2026-03-01.question: Which city will host the AI Summit 2027, as announced?
2026-03-01.explanation: Geneva will host the AI Summit 2027, marking Switzerland’s significant role in advancing global dialogue on artificial intelligence governance. The announcement was made by Swiss President Guy Parmelin during the AI Impact Summit in New Delhi. Known for being a hub of major international organisations, Geneva provides a neutral platform for multilateral discussions and cooperation. The summit is expected to focus on ethical and inclusive AI frameworks, strengthening partnerships between countries such as Switzerland and India. The hosting also reflects growing global collaboration in AI diplomacy, with the UAE set to host the summit in 2028.

2026-03-01.question: Which organisation successfully conducted three flight trials of the indigenous VSHORADS missile system, making it ready for induction into the Indian armed forces?
2026-03-01.explanation: DRDO successfully carried out three consecutive flight trials of the indigenous VSHORADS missile system from Chandipur, Odisha, demonstrating its operational readiness. The Very Short Range Air Defence System is a man-portable missile designed to intercept low-flying aircraft, helicopters, drones, and high-speed aerial threats. Developed under the Aatmanirbhar Bharat initiative, the system was tested in its final deployment configuration with trained field operators handling target acquisition and firing. Data from telemetry, radar, and electro-optical tracking confirmed its precision and effectiveness, strengthening India’s short-range and layered air defence capabilities significantly.

2026-03-01.question: Which former India captain will have a stand named after him at Mumbai’s Wankhede Stadium?
2026-03-01.explanation: Ravi Shastri will have a stand named after him at the iconic Wankhede Stadium in Mumbai following approval by the Mumbai Cricket Association during its Apex Council meeting. The Level 1 Stand below the Press Box will bear his name, recognising his long and multifaceted contribution to Indian cricket as a player, captain, head coach, and commentator. A former all-rounder, he was part of India’s 1983 World Cup era and later guided the national team to significant overseas Test victories as coach. The tribute highlights Mumbai’s rich cricketing legacy and honours his enduring association with the sport.

2026-03-01.question: On which date will World NGO Day 2026 be observed globally?
2026-03-01.explanation: February 27 is observed globally as World NGO Day in 2026, recognizing the vital contributions of non-governmental organisations across sectors such as education, healthcare, environmental protection, human rights, and disaster relief. The day serves as an international platform to appreciate NGOs for their grassroots efforts and to promote awareness, advocacy, and collaboration. It highlights the role of civil society in addressing social inequalities, poverty reduction, and sustainable development. The observance encourages citizens, institutions, and governments to actively participate through volunteering, donations, partnerships, and community initiatives that strengthen the global NGO ecosystem.

2026-02-28.question: Which company secured a ₹36 crore order to supply fabricated steel products for a BHEL project?
2026-02-28.explanation: BMW Ventures Limited secured a ₹36 crore contract to supply fabricated steel products for a major project executed by Bharat Heavy Electricals Limited (BHEL). The order signifies the company’s strategic expansion into large-scale infrastructure and power sector projects, moving beyond its traditional operational scope. The contract includes the supply of structural steel fabrication and related critical components essential for thermal or industrial infrastructure initiatives. The execution timeline is estimated at 12–18 months, enhancing the company’s order book strength, revenue visibility, and positioning within India’s rapidly growing infrastructure and energy sector.

2026-02-28.question: Which vessel was commissioned as the fourth ship of the Anti-Submarine Warfare Shallow Water Craft (ASW-SWC) project into the Indian Navy in February 2026?
2026-02-28.explanation: INS Anjadip was commissioned into the Indian Navy on 27 February 2026 at Chennai Port as the fourth ship under the Anti-Submarine Warfare Shallow Water Craft project. The ceremony was presided over by the Chief of the Naval Staff, marking a major boost to India’s littoral and coastal defence capabilities. The 77-meter vessel, with a displacement of 1,400 tons, is specially designed for shallow-water anti-submarine operations. With over 80% indigenous content, including defence electronics and weapon systems, it highlights India’s strong commitment to self-reliance in defence manufacturing and maritime security preparedness.

2026-02-28.question: Which country launched the ‘Zero Prize’, the first-ever results-based environmental award aimed at reducing pollution?
2026-02-28.explanation: India launched the ‘Zero Prize’ as the country’s first results-based environmental award focused on achieving measurable reductions in air, water, and land pollution. The initiative carries a total corpus of ₹5 crore, with ₹1 crore allocated to each of the three categories. It emphasises verified and quantifiable outcomes through third-party audits and scientific monitoring rather than mere declarations or planned actions. The award aligns with broader national initiatives such as Mission LiFE, Swachh Bharat, and net-zero ambitions, promoting accountability and outcome-driven environmental governance across multiple sectors.

2026-02-28.question: Which country’s central bank launched the world’s first sovereign financial cloud platform called “Financial Cloud”?
2026-02-28.explanation: The UAE launched the world’s first sovereign financial cloud platform through its Central Bank, marking a significant milestone in digital financial infrastructure. The platform, named Financial Cloud, is a fully regulated and secure cloud environment exclusively designed for licensed financial institutions within the country. It ensures strict compliance with data sovereignty, cybersecurity, and regulatory standards while allowing institutions to host critical workloads and applications. The initiative supports the nation’s broader vision of becoming a global fintech and digital economy hub under UAE Vision 2031 and the Dubai Economic Agenda D33, reducing dependence on global hyperscalers.

2026-02-28.question: Which Indian airport signed a cargo partnership MoU with Frankfurt Airport to enhance air cargo connectivity between Europe and India?
2026-02-28.explanation: Kempegowda International Airport entered into a strategic cargo partnership with Frankfurt Airport to strengthen air cargo connectivity between Europe and India. The Memorandum of Understanding was signed on 25 February 2026 on the sidelines of Air Cargo India 2026 in Mumbai. The collaboration focuses on digitalisation, regulatory optimisation, pharma cargo integrity standards, joint trade lane analytics, and knowledge exchange. This partnership aims to create a more integrated and efficient cargo corridor, reduce dwell times, enhance predictability for airlines and freight forwarders, and support the growing trade volumes between the two regions.

2026-02-28.question: Which country did the Indian delegation visit to advance cooperation on transboundary rivers and hydropower projects in February 2026?
2026-02-28.explanation: Bhutan was the country visited by an Indian delegation led by the Secretary of the Department of Water Resources, River Development & Ganga Rejuvenation to strengthen cooperation on trans-boundary river management and hydropower projects. The discussions included reviewing ongoing joint initiatives, enhancing hydro-meteorological data sharing, improving flood forecasting systems, and addressing climate-related challenges such as glacial lake outburst floods and extreme weather events. The engagement reinforced the long-standing hydropower partnership between the two nations, which dates back to 1961 and was further strengthened through a bilateral agreement signed in 2006, emphasising sustainable and mutually beneficial resource management.

2026-02-28.question: From which date has the Government of India mandated the nationwide sale of E20 petrol with a minimum RON 95 at all retail outlets?
2026-02-28.explanation: 1 April 2026 marks the official nationwide rollout of E20 petrol with a minimum Research Octane Number (RON) of 95 across all petrol pumps in India. The mandate requires every retail outlet, including public sector units and private oil marketing companies, to replace regular E10 petrol with E20 as the standard grade. This move is a major milestone under the Ethanol Blending Programme aimed at reducing crude oil imports, lowering carbon emissions, supporting farmers through higher ethanol demand, and enhancing engine performance with higher-octane fuel. Higher ethanol blends and special fuels remain outside this mandate.

2026-02-28.question: Who was appointed as the Managing Director & Chief Executive Officer (MD & CEO) of Hindustan Oil Exploration Company Limited (HOEC) effective 27 February 2026?
2026-02-28.explanation: Baroruchi Mishra was appointed as the Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of Hindustan Oil Exploration Company Limited (HOEC), effective 27 February 2026. He succeeded Ramasamy Jeevanandam, who had served in the role since 2019 and stepped down as part of the leadership transition. Mishra brings significant expertise in upstream oil and gas operations, with extensive experience in exploration, production, and business development across Indian and multinational energy firms. His appointment marks an important strategic development for HOEC as it continues to strengthen its position in the independent upstream energy sector.

2026-02-28.question: What was India’s global rank among 84 countries in mental health and well-being for young adults (18–34 years) according to the Global Mind Health 2025 report?
2026-02-28.explanation: 60th rank was secured by India among 84 countries in the Global Mind Health 2025 assessment focusing on young adults aged 18–34 years. The ranking places the country in the lower-middle tier globally, highlighting significant mental health challenges such as stress, anxiety, depression, and loneliness among youth. The report, prepared by the Sapien Labs Centre for the Future of Mental Health, is based on responses from over one million adults using the Mental Health Quotient (MHQ) tool. It emphasises socioeconomic pressures, cultural stigma, limited access to care, and modern lifestyle factors influencing declining mental well-being among younger generations.

2026-02-28.question: Which Indian state launched ‘Operation Crackdown’ to dismantle organised cybercrime networks?
2026-02-28.explanation: Telangana initiated ‘Operation Crackdown’ as a statewide, multi-agency drive to aggressively target and dismantle organised cybercrime networks. The campaign focuses on offences such as call centre fraud, digital arrest scams, investment fraud, sextortion, and job fraud. Led by the Telangana Police Cyber Security Bureau in coordination with local police, CID, SIT, and other specialised units, the operation involves coordinated raids, arrests, asset seizures, and intelligence-based actions across districts. The initiative aims to disrupt the entire cybercrime ecosystem, from front-end fraudsters to financial handlers, reinforcing a strict zero-tolerance approach toward cyber offenders.

2026-02-28.question: Which country imposed a temporary ban on poultry meat and table egg imports from India and 39 other nations as a precaution against avian influenza?
2026-02-28.explanation: Saudi Arabia imposed a temporary ban on the import of poultry meat and table eggs from 40 countries, including India, as a preventive measure to safeguard public health. The decision was announced by the Saudi Food and Drug Authority (SFDA) following global risk assessments and reported outbreaks of highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) and Newcastle disease. The restriction excludes heat-treated or fully processed poultry products that meet SFDA certification standards. Additionally, partial restrictions were placed on specific regions in 16 other countries, with authorities committing to periodic reviews and updates based on evolving disease situations worldwide.

2026-02-27.question: Which state government launched the Banglar Yuva Sathi Scheme 2026 to provide monthly financial assistance to unemployed youth?
2026-02-27.explanation: West Bengal launched the Banglar Yuva Sathi Scheme 2026 to provide ₹1,500 per month to eligible unemployed youth aged 21–40 years through Direct Benefit Transfer into Aadhaar-linked bank accounts. The scheme offers support for up to five years or until beneficiaries secure employment or self-employment. Announced during the interim budget for 2026–27 and administered by the Department of Sports and Youth Services, it aims to provide interim financial relief amid rising joblessness. With a significant budget allocation and large-scale registrations, the initiative targets lakhs of beneficiaries across the state.

2026-02-27.question: Who has been appointed as the Chief People Officer of OpenAI to lead its HR functions?
2026-02-27.explanation: OpenAI appointed Arvind KC as its new Chief People Officer to oversee key human resource functions such as hiring, onboarding, and employee development. His appointment comes at a time when the organisation is experiencing rapid global expansion following the widespread success of ChatGPT and other AI products. Arvind KC brings significant experience from senior leadership roles at major technology companies, including Roblox, Google, Palantir Technologies, and Meta Platforms. His expertise in scaling high-growth technology firms and managing large workforces positions him to support OpenAI’s expanding operations and workforce development strategies.

2026-02-27.question: Which state launched the Homestay (Paying Guest House) Scheme 2026 to promote rural tourism and self-employment?
2026-02-27.explanation: The Rajasthan Homestay (Paying Guest House) Scheme 2026 was introduced to decentralise tourism and stimulate rural economic growth. The initiative encourages self-employment, particularly among women and small investors, while offering tourists authentic local cultural experiences. The scheme features a fully digital and simplified registration process aligned with Ease of Doing Business and Ease of Living priorities. It increases accommodation capacity, removes the mandatory owner-residence requirement, and provides faster approvals, including deemed approval provisions. With silver and gold registration categories and statewide implementation, the scheme broadens participation and strengthens Rajasthan’s rural tourism infrastructure.

2026-02-27.question: What is the primary objective of the nationwide HPV vaccination campaign launched in February 2026?
2026-02-27.explanation: To prevent cervical cancer is the primary objective of the nationwide HPV vaccination campaign launched by the Government of India. The initiative targets 14-year-old girls and provides a free single dose of the Gardasil 4 vaccine, which protects against high-risk HPV types 16 and 18 responsible for most cervical cancer cases, as well as types 6 and 11. Cervical cancer remains one of the leading causes of cancer-related deaths among women in India. By focusing on early immunization, the campaign emphasizes preventive healthcare, aiming to significantly reduce future cancer incidence and mortality rates across the country.

2026-02-27.question: When is International Polar Bear Day observed every year to raise awareness about polar bear conservation?
2026-02-27.explanation: February 27 is observed annually as International Polar Bear Day to highlight the urgent need for polar bear conservation and climate action. The date coincides with the critical denning period when polar bear mothers and their newborn cubs remain sheltered in snow dens, making them highly vulnerable. Organised by Polar Bears International, the day focuses on raising awareness about climate change, shrinking Arctic sea ice, and habitat loss. It promotes research, education, and policy advocacy aimed at protecting polar bear populations and ensuring the survival of future generations in the rapidly warming Arctic region.

2026-02-27.question: Which institute signed an MoU with NMDC’s R&D Centre to advance mineral processing and green technologies?
2026-02-27.explanation: IIT Hyderabad entered into a Memorandum of Understanding with NMDC’s R&D Centre to promote long-term academic and industry collaboration in mineral and metals research. The partnership integrates NMDC’s practical field expertise with the institute’s academic strength and technological innovation. The collaboration focuses on critical areas such as iron ore beneficiation, green steelmaking technologies, alternate ironmaking processes using indigenous raw materials, and advanced modeling and simulation in mining and metallurgy. This initiative aims to support India’s mineral security, encourage sustainable industrial practices, and enhance self-reliance in strategic materials through research-driven solutions.

2026-02-27.question: After whom will Pakyong Airport in Sikkim be renamed to honour his contribution to India’s freedom struggle?
2026-02-27.explanation: Trilochan Pokhrel is being honoured through the renaming of Pakyong Airport in Sikkim in recognition of his significant role in India’s freedom movement. Popularly known as “Gandhi Pokhrel,” he is regarded as Sikkim’s first independence activist and actively participated in major national movements such as the Non-Cooperation Movement, Civil Disobedience Movement, and Quit India Movement. Inspired by Mahatma Gandhi, he worked to spread nationalist ideas within Sikkim. The renaming symbolises the state’s effort to preserve its historical legacy and acknowledge local heroes who contributed to India’s independence.

2026-02-27.question: Which Argentine player won his maiden ATP 500 title at the Rio Open by defeating Alejandro Tabilo in the final?
2026-02-27.explanation: Tomas Martin Etcheverry secured his first ATP Tour title and the biggest victory of his career at the Rio Open ATP 500 event in Brazil. The 26-year-old Argentine defeated Alejandro Tabilo in a hard-fought three-set final, demonstrating resilience after overcoming a rain-delayed schedule and winning two crucial matches on the same day. This triumph marked a breakthrough moment following three previous runner-up finishes. The victory significantly improved his global ranking, pushing him up 18 places to World No. 33 and returning him to the Top 40, strengthening his position ahead of the clay-court season.

2026-02-27.question: Which location hosted Exercise Kalari Leap led by Southern Air Command?
2026-02-27.explanation: Exercise Kalari Leap was conducted as a high-impact joint maritime operation led by the Southern Air Command in coordination with the Armed Forces Special Operations Division and the Indian Coast Guard. The exercise took place in the Lakshadweep and Minicoy islands, focusing on rapid force projection, precision strikes, and multi-domain coordination in a challenging maritime environment. It aimed to validate operational readiness, enhance interoperability among forces, and strengthen India’s maritime security posture. The operation highlighted the importance of jointness, technological integration, and swift response capabilities in strategically significant island territories.

2026-02-27.question: Which company launched an AI-powered natural language search feature built on Microsoft Foundry in February 2026?
2026-02-27.explanation: PhonePe introduced an AI-powered natural language search feature on 20 February 2026, leveraging Microsoft Foundry to enhance user experience within its application. The feature allows users to perform tasks such as payments, recharges, navigation, and transaction tracking through simple voice or text-based commands. By using intent-based queries, the platform transitions from a purely transactional interface to a more intelligent and personalised system. Built on a hybrid on-device and cloud model, the solution ensures data security while improving accessibility, convenience, and discoverability for millions of users across India through a phased rollout.

2026-02-26.question: What is the primary objective of the ‘Blockchain India Challenge’ launched by MeitY?
2026-02-26.explanation: To Boost Digital Governance is the central objective behind the launch of the ‘Blockchain India Challenge’ by the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology. The initiative encourages Indian startups to build secure, permissioned blockchain solutions tailored for government use cases. It focuses on enhancing regulatory control, transparency, auditability, and tamper-proof record management across sectors such as healthcare, agriculture, education, land records, and public distribution systems. Implemented with support from C-DAC, the programme provides stage-wise funding to selected startups, aiming to create scalable, field-ready solutions that strengthen efficiency and trust in public service delivery systems across India.

2026-02-26.question: Under which Article of the Constitution can Parliament alter the name, area, or boundaries of a State, as in the proposal to rename Kerala as “Keralam”?
2026-02-26.explanation: Article 3 of the Constitution empowers Parliament to alter the name, area, or boundaries of a State by law. In the case of renaming Kerala as “Keralam,” the constitutional procedure requires the President to refer the Bill to the concerned State Legislature for expressing its views. After receiving those views, the Central Government may proceed to introduce the Bill in Parliament with the President’s recommendation. The proposal also involves amending the First Schedule of the Constitution, where the names of States are officially listed, ensuring that any change follows due constitutional process.

2026-02-26.question: In which city will the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change organise ‘Him-CONNECT’ during WSDS 2026?
2026-02-26.explanation: New Delhi is the host city for ‘Him-CONNECT’, which will be organised by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change on the sidelines of the World Sustainable Development Summit 2026. The platform aims to connect researchers from the Indian Himalayan Region with startups, investors, and policymakers to scale climate-resilient innovations. More than 24 technologies developed under the National Mission on Himalayan Studies will be showcased, focusing on water security, renewable energy, waste-to-wealth solutions, sustainable building, and nature-based livelihoods, reinforcing India’s commitment to sustainable mountain development and climate action.

2026-02-26.question: What Minimum Support Price (MSP) has been approved for Raw Jute (TD-3 grade) for the 2026-27 marketing season?
2026-02-26.explanation: ₹5,925 is the Minimum Support Price approved for Raw Jute (TD-3 grade) for the 2026-27 marketing season. The decision was taken by the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs to ensure better remuneration for jute farmers.
